findings.finding: The bar looks low against the company's own trajectory. Consensus Q3 EBITA of 59.7m (4.95% margin) is below last year's adjusted Q3 EBITA of 62.5m (5.1%), while Q2 2026 adjusted EBITA rose 14% YoY to 61.5m on comparable sales of -0.9%, utilisation has improved for over a year, and headcount is ~5% lower (3,550 vs 3,732).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: reported EBITA 77.4 vs 43 expected, +13.75%. Q2 2026: reported EBITA 23.0 vs 45 expected but adjusted 61.5 up 14%, +6.29%. Q1 2026: EBITA ~16% under, -18.76%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus was compiled on 2026-10-20 and sits below last year's adjusted level. If the market priced a margin step-up, the 4-contributor bar would sit above 62.5m rather than at 59.7m. The stock is +5.7% over 20 days, which is modest beside its ±13-19% report-day moves.

findings.finding: The new CEO's 2 Sep country-led reorganisation (three Group Management members out, two leaving the company, effective 1 Oct) will probably put restructuring or severance one-offs into Q3 reported EBITA. That risks a 'lower than expected' headline against the 59.7m consensus, as in Q2 when reported EBITA was 23.0 vs 45. Peer Columbus booked a DKK 20m severance provision in Q3 for an AI-driven capacity cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: CEO-exit costs of 38.5m made reported EBITA miss by 49%, and the stock still rose 6.29% because adjusted EBITA rose. The market has looked through items affecting comparability here.
findings.why_not_priced: The reorganisation is public, but its cost is not quantified anywhere. The consensus release does not say whether the 59.7m EBITA includes it, so the first Finwire headline may compare reported EBITA with a clean bar.
